title: COM11 — Plan an ad

slides.title: Planning starts with the reader
slides.body:
Audience → message → action

State who will see the ad and what they should do.

The independent ad uses an actual approved school/community message.
slides.alt: Planning starts with the reader — labelled teaching visual
slides.definition: State who will see the ad and what they should do.
slides.example: The independent ad uses an actual approved school/community message.
slides.notes: Before choosing pictures or fonts, identify a particular reader, viewing setting and next action. Those facts guide your design choices. Planning is visible reasoning, not a requirement to decorate a page. Our worked café material is constructed practice; your independent message must be real and approved. Write your audience and intended action in one sentence.

slides.task: Write: My audience is __. After viewing, I want them to __.

slides.title: Build the mood board in your browser
slides.body:
Images + colour + type + tone

Curate references and explain their purpose.

A board should help someone discuss the proposed direction.
slides.lead: Free Excalidraw editor · no installation or account
slides.alt: A mood board proposes a direction — labelled teaching visual
slides.definition: Arrange an image, colour roles, type samples and reasons.
slides.example: Keep an editable .excalidraw master and a review PNG.
slides.notes: Use the free editor at excalidraw.com. Its MIT-licensed source is public. No installation or account was needed for this worked board. The image is an original practice illustration. The board combines a reference, labelled colour roles, type specimens and an audience-based reason. Open the linked browser lab for action screenshots. Save an editable scene and a PNG rather than relying on shared browser storage. School access and disk-save/reopen still need verification.

slides.title: An artboard is a canvas inside the file
slides.body:
One Photoshop document, several layouts

Keep a PNG mood reference, option A and option B together.

Artboards contain their own layers and clip content at their edges.
slides.alt: An artboard is a canvas inside the file — labelled teaching visual
slides.definition: Keep a PNG mood reference, option A and option B together.
slides.example: Artboards contain their own layers and clip content at their edges.
slides.notes: A Photoshop artboard is a named canvas inside one document. The mood board describes a visual direction; an artboard is the place you can put that board or a sketch. Build the mood board in the free Excalidraw browser editor, keep its editable master, then place a PNG reference on 01_MOOD. We will keep three named boards together. A layer holds an element inside a board. Selecting the board group matters when you change its size or add content.

slides.title: Explain the difference
slides.body:
Direction and arrangement answer different questions

Mood: what should it feel like? Sketch: where does information go?

You can create both on artboards.
slides.lead: Direction and arrangement answer different questions
slides.alt: Explain the difference — labelled teaching visual
slides.definition: Mood: what should it feel like? Sketch: where does information go?
slides.example: You can create both on artboards.
slides.notes: Check the distinction individually. A palette, image references and type samples propose a direction. Boxes for headline, image, detail and action propose an arrangement. Photoshop artboards can hold either. Calling a mood board an artboard confuses the purpose of the content with the container. After answering, explain your choice in your own words.
slides.narration: Check the distinction individually. A palette, image references and type samples propose a direction. Boxes for headline, image, detail and action propose an arrangement. Photoshop artboards can hold either. Calling a mood board an artboard confuses the purpose of the content with the container. After answering, explain your choice in your own words.

options: A mood board is a visual direction; an artboard is a canvas.
A mood board is the final published ad.
Every layer is a separate artboard.
quiz.why: Purpose and container are different: an artboard can hold a mood board or a layout sketch.

slides.native_question: Choose: A direction/canvas; B final ad; C every layer. Explain.

slides.title: Translate a reference into a choice
slides.body:
Visible feature → idea → reason

Study one feature; design an original response.

Record creator/source and permission.
slides.alt: Translate a reference into a choice — labelled teaching visual
slides.definition: Study one feature; design an original response.
slides.notes: These are actual campaign images from the main teaching deck. Study the simplified directional mark in Follow the Arches, the image and action relationship in Recycle Me, and the expressive typography in the Public Theater example. A feature may inspire an original decision, or conflict with your intended tone. Credit the reference and explain the connection. Do not copy the brand or assume that a visible design proves audience effects. Your final ad needs original or permitted assets.

slides.task: Name one reference feature and explain why it might serve your reader.

slides.title: Give colour and type clear roles
slides.body:
Background · message · accent

Annotate roles instead of listing favourites.

Keep words readable; the palette label does not prove contrast.
slides.alt: Give colour and type clear roles — labelled teaching visual
slides.definition: Annotate roles instead of listing favourites.
slides.example: Keep words readable; the palette label does not prove contrast.
slides.notes: In Excalidraw, Rectangle creates a swatch and Background opens its fill colour. The actual worked values are cream f4ead5, dark ink 193443 and terracotta b85a36. The labels explain background, main words and accent roles. These are practice choices, not an independent solution. Add headline and detail specimens; the browser font does not guarantee the same font exists in Photoshop. Test final readability in the intended viewing setting.

slides.title: Check both artboard dimensions
slides.body:
1080 × 1350 px for this digital practice

Use File → New, with Artboards enabled.

Genuine capture shows an incorrect inherited H 2400. Correction is pending.
slides.alt: Check both artboard dimensions — labelled teaching visual
slides.definition: Use File → New, with Artboards enabled.
slides.example: Genuine capture shows an incorrect inherited H 2400. Correction is pending.
slides.notes: This is a genuine capture from our first setup attempt. Width became 1080, but the inherited height stayed 2400. The lesson is to read both pixel dimensions before and after creation. Resolution 72 PPI and RGB colour do not repair the wrong height. The corrective native demonstration is still pending; your teacher must verify the procedure before classroom use.

slides.title: Diagnose the setup mistake
slides.body:
Read the values, then target the cause

The requested frame is 1080 × 1350.

Select the artboard; inspect W and H in Properties.
slides.lead: Read the values, then target the cause
slides.alt: Diagnose the setup mistake — labelled teaching visual
slides.example: Select the artboard; inspect W and H in Properties.
slides.notes: Diagnose the actual mistake. A tall artboard was created because the height field did not change. The proposed repair is to select the artboard group and set its H property to 1350. That repair has not yet been captured or tested here. Changing a type layer or altering only PPI would not address this cause. Explain why your chosen repair targets the mismatch.
slides.narration: Diagnose the actual mistake. A tall artboard was created because the height field did not change. The proposed repair is to select the artboard group and set its H property to 1350. That repair has not yet been captured or tested here. Changing a type layer or altering only PPI would not address this cause. Explain why your chosen repair targets the mismatch.

quiz.q: The frame is 1080 × 2400 instead of 1080 × 1350. What should you inspect?
quiz.why: The mismatch is the artboard pixel height. Confirm the board is selected, set H to 1350 and recheck.

slides.native_question: Check: A artboard height; B text tracking; C PPI only. Explain.

slides.title: Sketch before polishing
slides.body:
Compare two different reading orders

Use boxes and short labels for the important parts.

Keep the brief, copy, palette and size fixed.
slides.alt: Sketch before polishing — labelled teaching visual
slides.definition: Use boxes and short labels for the important parts.
slides.example: Keep the brief, copy, palette and size fixed.
slides.notes: A thumbnail is a low-cost layout hypothesis. Option A may lead with a headline, while B may lead with an image. Keep the same essential information and size so the comparison is meaningful. In Photoshop use editable shape and text layers, or import paper thumbnails. Do not begin with effects or detailed retouching. The question is whether the reader finds the message and action.

Do not begin with effects or detailed retouching. The question is whether the reader finds the message and action.
slides.task: Make A and B differ in hierarchy. Predict first → second → third for each.

slides.title: Ask a reader without coaching the answer
slides.body:
Notice → message → action

Show A and B at the same size.

Record their actual words separately from your prediction.
slides.alt: Ask a reader without coaching the answer — labelled teaching visual
slides.definition: Show A and B at the same size.
slides.example: Record their actual words separately from your prediction.
slides.notes: Ask what the reader noticed first, what the message was, and what they would do next. Avoid telling them what you intended before they respond. Record what happened, even when it disagrees with your prediction. If you have no reader, label the record self-check. A fair comparison and honest observation provide a reason for a revision; invented praise does not.

slides.title: Preserve the first idea and revise
slides.body:
One problem → one purposeful change

Keep A and B; duplicate the chosen direction.

Retest the change, then explain a tradeoff.
slides.alt: Preserve the first idea and revise — labelled teaching visual
slides.definition: Keep A and B; duplicate the chosen direction.
slides.example: Retest the change, then explain a tradeoff.
slides.notes: Keep the two initial sketches. Duplicate the direction you choose and change one feature connected to an observed problem. Retest with neutral questions. Explain the benefit and anything the change makes harder. If your teacher changes the audience or viewing setting, decide what you would retain and what you would change. The purpose is independent judgement, not copying the worked model.

slides.task: Which feature would you change after feedback, and why?

slides.title: Show the reasoning and the files
slides.body:
Direction → alternatives → evidence → revision

Keep an editable PSD and review exports.

Native save/reopen and the independent cold run remain pending.
slides.alt: Show the reasoning and the files — labelled teaching visual
slides.definition: Keep .excalidraw + PNG, a layered Photoshop PSD and review exports.
slides.example: Browser disk-save/reopen and the native Photoshop workflow remain pending.
slides.notes: Keep the browser mood board as an editable .excalidraw scene and a review PNG. Bring the PNG into 01_MOOD as a reference, then make two editable Photoshop layout sketches. quiz.q: Which evidence best supports a revision?
options: A reader response linked to a visible change
A checklist saying every tutorial step was completed
quiz.why: Explain what the reader observed, what you changed and what the retest showed. Files and completion checks alone do not establish communication quality.

slides.native_question: Evidence: A reader response + visible change; B completed steps; C file size. Explain.
